title: Asked to Digitally Sign a PDF? Check Whether a Certificate Is Required
description: If someone asks you to digitally sign a PDF, confirm whether they accept a visible electronic signature or require a certificate-based digital signature.
direct: If someone asks you to digitally sign a PDF, confirm whether they accept a visible electronic signature or require a certificate-based digital signature. A signature drawn on a page does not by itself provide certificate validation.

cards.choice.heading: Ask about the deliverable
cards.choice.body: A visible electronic signature can communicate acceptance. A certificate-based digital signature also provides a way to verify signing credentials and detect certain changes. The recipient’s process decides which form they need; visual appearance alone does not establish acceptance.
sections.explain.heading: Finish edits before certificate signing
sections.explain.body: Merging, compressing or rearranging an already digitally signed PDF can change the signed document and affect validation. Keep the signed original and ask the issuer for the correct workflow rather than flattening it to preserve only the visible signature image.
sections.practice.heading: Know the app boundary
sections.practice.body: Space Sheep Studio develops PDF Compressor for iPhone. Its current listing includes PDF signing, compression, scanning and merging, but does not establish certificate issuance, qualified signatures or signature-validation services. Try any export tool once free; further exports require Pro. This is a file-workflow distinction, not a statement that a particular signature satisfies a jurisdiction, contract or recipient’s policy. Confirm the required process before sending.

steps.step-1.text: Ask the recipient which signing method and file checks their workflow requires before editing the document.
steps.step-2.text: If an ordinary visible signature is accepted, use the signing tool in PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge and save a separate copy.
steps.step-3.text: Open the saved PDF and inspect placement and page completeness. If a certificate is required, use the recipient’s specified certificate-signing process instead.
